title: Task Admin bulk actions
problem: Operators had to action queue items one at a time, making large workloads slow and error-prone.
evidence: 78% of tested users expected select-all behavior; task completion time averaged 4.2 min for batch work.
recommendation: Introduce multi-select with a bulk action bar and clear selection state before building further queue features.
outcome: Blocked downstream queue work until the interaction model is agreed; prototype validated with the ops panel.

title: Search date-range filtering
problem: Users could not filter account search results by date range, forcing manual scanning of long lists.
evidence: Backend limitation surfaced during research; 6 of 8 participants abandoned the task.
recommendation: Resolve the indexing constraint before shipping the redesigned filter panel.
outcome: Flagged as a blocker to the search redesign; engineering scoping in progress.

title: AI response confidence labels
problem: Users could not judge how much to trust AI responses, reducing adoption of the assistant.
evidence: Panel sessions showed hesitation and repeated manual verification of AI output.
recommendation: Add confidence labels, reasoning surfaces, and fallback states to an already-shipping surface.
outcome: Enhanced a live experience; trust and repeat usage improved in follow-up testing.

title: Onboarding flow rework
problem: Account creation had a high drop-off rate, limiting activation of new users.
evidence: Funnel analysis showed a 34% drop at the verification step.
recommendation: Rework the step sequencing and guidance on the current onboarding flow.
outcome: Enhanced a high-traffic flow; drop-off reduced in the redesigned path.

title: Quantifying UX dashboard
problem: Leadership had no consistent way to see UX's contribution, so its impact stayed invisible in planning conversations.
evidence: Monthly reviews relied on anecdotes; there was no shared view of research coverage, delivery, and influence.
recommendation: Build a single dashboard that quantifies UX contribution across research, delivery, and business impact.
outcome: Enhanced how leadership sees UX; contribution is now legible and tracked month over month.

title: Making the design system AI-ready
problem: AI-assisted design and vibe-coded prototypes drift from the system because the token layer alone carries values, not the reasoning behind them — so agents make logical-but-wrong choices.
evidence: Components meant to be identical diverge across screens and sessions; agents can read a token's value but not when or why to use it, or how components relate.
recommendation: Structure the system in three layers: a token layer (the raw values), an intent layer (what each token means and when to use it), and a guardrail layer (rules and design.md docs that constrain agent decisions).
outcome: An early opportunity to make the system agent-ready, cutting AI-generated design debt and keeping output consistent across separate sessions.

title: Prompt builder zero-state
problem: New users faced an empty prompt builder with no guidance on where to start.
evidence: Early concept testing surfaced confusion and low first-session success.
recommendation: Explore zero-state patterns and example prompts as a new capability.
outcome: A new opportunity to improve first-run experience; concept validated for further investment.

title: Risk communication patterns
problem: Users felt anxious interpreting risk information presented in technical language.
evidence: Qualitative sessions surfaced repeated confusion and elevated task stress.
recommendation: Prototype plain-language risk patterns as a new, unmet-need direction.
outcome: An opportunity to reduce user anxiety; early patterns tested positively.

title: Transact panel groupings
problem: Dense transaction screens forced heavy scrolling, slowing operators during high-volume work.
evidence: Session recordings showed repeated long scrolls to reach common panels; task time suffered.
recommendation: Regroup transaction panels by frequency and task, collapsing rarely used sections to reduce scrolling.
outcome: An optimization that cut scrolling and sped up common transaction tasks.

title: Cross-product design tokens
problem: Inconsistent spacing and color across products slowed delivery and review.
evidence: Audit found 40+ divergent values for the same intent across teams.
recommendation: Standardize a shared token set to simplify and speed up existing work.
outcome: An optimization that reduced rework and sped up handoff across teams.

title: Notification center consolidation
problem: Notifications were spread across surfaces, adding noise and maintenance overhead.
evidence: Support tickets cited duplicate and conflicting alerts.
recommendation: Consolidate into one center to simplify the existing experience.
outcome: An optimization that simplified the surface and reduced duplicate alerts.
